question_text:
We produce a 10 -in.-long bimetallic composite material composed of a strip of yellow brass bonded to a strip of Invar. Determine the length to which each material would expand when the temperature increases from $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $150^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Draw a sketch showing what will happen to the shape of the bimetallic strip.

Give your answer as a tuple: (brass_length_in, invar_length_in).The units of each required answer are (in, in), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

For a bimetallic strip, each material tries to expand by its own amount:

$$\Delta L = \alpha \, L_0 \, \Delta T$$

with $L_0 = 10\ \text{in}$ and $\Delta T = 150 - 20 = 130^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.

Using standard CTE values:
- **Yellow brass:** $\alpha = 20.5\times10^{-6}\ /^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$
- **Invar (64Fe–36Ni):** $\alpha = 1.3\times10^{-6}\ /^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$

**Brass:**
$$\Delta L_{\text{brass}} = (20.5\times10^{-6})(10)(130) = 0.02665\ \text{in}$$
$$L_{\text{brass}} = 10.02665\ \text{in}$$

**Invar:**
$$\Delta L_{\text{invar}} = (1.3\times10^{-6})(10)(130) = 0.00169\ \text{in}$$
$$L_{\text{invar}} = 10.00169\ \text{in}$$

### Sketch — shape of the bimetallic strip

Since brass expands far more than Invar but the two are bonded, the strip cannot stay straight. The differential expansion forces the strip to **curve (bend)** into an arc, with:

- **Brass on the outer (convex) side** — it needs more length, so it stretches along the larger radius.
- **Invar on the inner (concave) side** — it stays shorter, along the smaller radius.

```
   20°C  (straight)            150°C  (curved)

   ┌───────────────┐           ╭───────────────╮
   │brass (top)    │    →      │ brass (outer) │
   │invar (bottom) │           │ invar (inner) │
   └───────────────┘           ╰───────────────╯
        10 in                    brass > invar
                                 strip bows upward
                                 (toward brass side)
```

The curvature develops because the bond constrains both strips to a common arc length at the interface; the brass (high α) goes into tension along the outer fiber and the Invar (low α) into compression along the inner fiber, producing a uniform bend.

$$\boxed{(10.02665,\ 10.00169)}$$
